question: To maintain blood glucose levels even after glycogen stores have been depleted, the body, mainly the liver, is able to synthesize glucose in a process called gluconeogenesis. Which of the following reactions of gluconeogenesis requires an enzyme different from glycolysis?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: 2-phosphoglycerate -> "converted to 3-phosphoglycerate" -> "uses the same enzyme as glycolysis" -> 85%
CHAIN: Fructose 1,6-bisphosphate -> "converted to Fructose-6-phosphate" -> "requires Fructose-1,6-bisphosphatase" -> "different enzyme from glycolysis" -> 95%
CHAIN: Phosphoenolpyruvate -> "converted to 2-phosphoglycerate" -> "uses the same enzyme as glycolysis" -> 80%
CHAIN: Dihydroxyacetone phosphate -> "converted to Glyceraldehyde 3-phosphate" -> "uses the same enzyme as glycolysis" -> 80%
CHAIN: 1,3-bisphosphoglycerate -> "converted to Glyceraldehyde 3-phosphate" -> "uses the same enzyme as glycolysis" -> 80%
analysis: In gluconeogenesis, certain steps require different enzymes than those used in glycolysis. The conversion of Fructose 1,6-bisphosphate to Fructose-6-phosphate is catalyzed by Fructose-1,6-bisphosphatase, which is not present in glycolysis. The other reactions listed either use the same enzymes as glycolysis or are reversible steps that do not require different enzymes.
